name: Dayan Old Town
description: The main old town and a UNESCO World Heritage site, Dayan is a maze of cobbled lanes, canals and wooden Naxi buildings radiating from Sifang Square and the Mu Palace. It is beautiful and atmospheric, but also the busiest and most touristy corner of the city.
bestFor: Culture seekers and first-time visitors who want to be in the heart of the old town
pros: Unmatched old-town atmosphere with canals, bridges and Naxi architecture
Everything within walking distance, from teahouses to bars
Rich culture around Sifang Square and the Mu Palace
cons: Very touristy, commercial and crowded, especially in peak season
Noisy bar streets and cobbles make it less practical for focused work

name: Shuhe Old Town
tagline: A quieter old town with room to breathe
description: A smaller, more relaxed old town a few kilometres northwest of Dayan, Shuhe shares the same cobbled lanes, streams and Naxi charm but with a calmer, less frantic pace. It has become a popular base for travellers who want old-town character without Dayan's density and noise.
bestFor: Nomads wanting old-town atmosphere with more calm and space to work
pros: Genuine old-town character with noticeably fewer crowds than Dayan
Pleasant cafes and guesthouses suited to longer stays
Easy access to Dayan and the surrounding countryside
cons: Fewer services and less nightlife than the main old town

name: New Town (Gucheng District)
description: The modern city surrounding the old towns, the new town in Gucheng district offers everyday conveniences: supermarkets, modern apartments, hospitals, banks and the main transport links. It lacks old-town charm but is cheaper, quieter for work and far more practical for a longer stay.
bestFor: Longer-term nomads prioritising value, space and reliable amenities
pros: Cheaper modern apartments and more space for the money
Full range of services, from supermarkets to hospitals
Closer to the railway station and transport hubs
cons: Little of the historic charm that draws people to Lijiang
Less walkable and atmospheric than the old towns

name: Baisha Village
tagline: The oldest Naxi settlement below the mountain
description: A tranquil village toward Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, Baisha is the oldest Naxi settlement in the area and once the Naxi capital. Known for its ancient frescoes and unhurried rural feel, it offers a glimpse of old Lijiang life with the mountain rising close on the horizon.
bestFor: Slow travellers and mountain lovers seeking quiet and authenticity
pros: Historic Baisha frescoes and traditional architecture
Closest base to Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and its trails
cons: Further from the city, so you rely on transport for daily needs
